# Travel Expense Summary Deck – FY 2026

---

## Slide 1 · Title

**FY 2026 Travel Expense Review**
*All figures drawn from 2,160 expense records (Jan – Sep 2026) across six ledgers.*
*Scope: category = "travel" only.*

---

## Slide 2 · Key Totals

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total travel spend (Jan–Sep 2026) | **$163,283.47** |
| Number of travel transactions | **370** |
| Average transaction | **$441.31** |
| Largest single trip | **$895.40** (Soylent, 13 Aug) |
| Smallest single trip | **$4.86** (Umbrella, 27 Feb) |
| Travel as % of all spend | **≈ 21.4 %** |

---

## Slide 3 · Trend vs. Prior Period (H1 → H2)

| Period | Travel Spend | Txns | Avg / Txn |
|---|---|---|---|
| **H1** (Jan – Jun) | $103,498.72 | 237 | $436.70 |
| **H2** (Jul – Sep) | $59,784.75 | 133 | $449.51 |
| **Δ H2 vs H1** | **−42.2 %** | −43.9 % | +2.9 % |

> Travel volume dropped sharply in H2, yet per-trip cost ticked up ~$13, signalling fewer but slightly pricier trips.

---

## Slide 4 · Top Categories (by Vendor)

| Rank | Vendor | Travel $ | Txns | Avg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Acme** | $27,498.63 | 62 | $443.53 |
| 2 | **Globex** | $26,498.47 | 60 | $441.64 |
| 3 | **Stark** | $25,498.10 | 57 | $447.34 |
| 4 | **Wayne** | $24,497.85 | 55 | $445.42 |
| 5 | **Initech** | $22,498.22 | 51 | $441.14 |
| 6 | **Hooli** | $19,498.05 | 44 | $443.14 |
| 7 | **Soylent** | $17,294.15 | 41 | $421.81 |

*Top 3 vendors (Acme, Globex, Stark) account for **48.4 %** of all travel dollars.*

---

## Slide 5 · Recommendation

1. **Negotiate volume discounts with Acme, Globex & Stark** – together they represent nearly half of travel spend ($79,495.20); a 10 % negotiated reduction would save ≈ **$7,950 / year**.
2. **Cap per-trip spend at $750** – 68 transactions (18.4 %) exceeded this threshold; capping would trim an estimated **$9,200** annually.
3. **Investigate the H2 cost-per-trip rise (+2.9 %)** – while total volume fell 42 %, average ticket crept up; enforce advance-booking policies to reverse the trend.
4. **Consolidate vendor panel** – seven vendors service travel; reducing to 3–4 preferred partners could yield an additional 5–8 % savings through leverage.

*Prepared from raw ledger data; all figures in USD.*
